sections.h2: What does the Robeson County Register of Deeds record in Lumberton?
sections.html:
Anything that transfers or encumbers land in Robeson County ends up here: the deed to your buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, the cancellation of your old loan, plats and similar papers. The county lists 910-671-3040 for questions about recordings.

The office is barred by state statute from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and it keeps no forms. Its recording page tells filers to see an attorney for any legal question and for drafting.

Why bother with the record at all? The recording rule in G.S. 47-18 works like a queue: a deed protects its holder against outside claims from the moment of registration locally, and earlier registration wins.

sections.h2: Why does Robeson County require tax certification before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Per the register's recording page, every deed needs tax certification before recording, unless it is accompanied by the delinquent tax statement under G.S. 161-31. A deed mailed without either one is returned to the sender.

The certification comes from the county tax department rather than the register. That makes the tax office the first stop for a Robeson deed, and it is the step sellers most often forget.

Ways to get a Robeson County deed certified by the tax office
MethodWhat the county says
EmailSend the documents to deeds@robesoncountync.gov
MailRobeson County Tax Department, 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton NC 28358
PhoneCall the tax office at 910-671-3060 for instructions

Ask your closing attorney whether the firm already requests certification for every deed it sends.

sections.h2: What else must be in place when a deed is recorded in person in Robeson County?
sections.html:
Every document recorded in person must show a return name and mailing address. No stamped, self-addressed envelope? A $1.00 mailing fee is added.

The paper must be drafted, signed and notarized before it arrives. Staff cannot repair a bad acknowledgment or write in missing terms.

  • Tax certification or the delinquent tax statement attached.
  • A return name and address on the document.
  • An envelope addressed to you with postage, or a dollar for the office to mail it.
  • The signed, notarized original.

Mailed packages follow the same rules, so include certification at the start. A call to 910-671-3040 can settle questions about a specific filing, and the county also hosts online deed search tools through its records page.

sections.h2: How are Robeson County recording fees set?
sections.html:
These are the statewide figures from G.S. 161-10, identical across North Carolina. Fifteen pages of an ordinary instrument cost $26 and each added page $4. Loan documents get 35 pages for $64. Recording a loan cancellation is free.

Plats cost $21 per sheet, a certified copy starts at $5 with $2 for each added page, and a document in nonstandard form adds $25. Each extra instrument in the same packet adds $10. These are paid before filing, so budget for them at closing, together with the mailing fee mentioned above if it applies.

sections.h2: Which side owes the deed excise tax in Robeson County?
sections.html:
The seller carries it. Under G.S. 105-228.30.

the transferor pays the register ahead of filing, at a dollar for each $500 of value with any fraction counted whole. Half remains with Robeson County. The remainder goes to the state revenue department every month after refunds, and the county may retain 2 percent of that state half. A parcel split between counties is taxed where more of its value sits.

The closing attorney should print the amount on your statement. If you want a figure early, tell the register's staff the sale price.

sections.h2: How do Robeson County property taxes affect a sale?
sections.html:
Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 owes for the year, and a sale later does not clear the seller's liability, the county tax office explains. Proration is a private agreement between buyer and seller, and the seller is mailed the bill for the year of transfer.

To be safe, ask for payment to the tax collector at closing. If the new bill is not yet due, the collector takes a prepayment based on the previous year's rate. A past-due bill on a property that sold during the year can result in both names being advertised.

The tax office that issues the certification is the same one to ask about your balance, so a single call can cover both.

sections.h2: Where do Robeson County parcel numbers and online payments come from?
sections.html:
The county tax administrator's Land Records and Mapping section assigns each tract a parcel identification number, which other county departments use for owner, acreage, value and zoning. The GIS and Addressing section sits in the same division. Quote the parcel number when you contact the tax office about certification, so staff can pull the right record.

The tax office also accepts online and phone payments. The county gives 1-866-249-0705 for the phone option and notes that a convenience fee applies.

  • Parcel number: ask the mapping section or find it on your tax bill.
  • Real property: listed permanently, so no annual listing is needed.
  • Bills: mailed in August and due September 1.

Before closing, make sure the tax figure the buyer's attorney requests matches what the collector tells you, since the seller is mailed the bill for the year of transfer. Keep the confirmation with your closing file, along with the certification the tax office gave for the deed.

sections.h2: What other filings can accompany a Robeson County sale?
sections.html:
A satisfaction clears your mortgage, and the office charges nothing to record it. Under G.S. 47-18, options, contracts to convey, leases past three years and rights of first refusal bind later buyers only when registered. Under Chapter 47H, an owner-financed contract for deed or a memorandum of it must be recorded within five business days.

  • Check that your payoff results in a recorded satisfaction.
  • Keep copies of every recorded paper.
  • Ask whether a plat or easement affects the lot.

A closing attorney can list every document headed to the register before the day arrives.

sections.h2: What can a Robeson County seller do now to speed recording?
sections.html:
Contact the tax office for certification as soon as the deed is drafted, not on closing day, because the certification has to be in hand before the register will accept the paper. Confirm that the deed carries a return address and that an envelope or postage is ready.

Then follow up with the register to confirm the book and page after filing, and ask the title company or attorney for a copy of the recorded deed for your own files. Keep the receipt for fees and the excise tax, and file it with your closing papers. If anything is returned to you, read the reason first, because the usual causes are missing tax certification or a missing return address.

faqs.q: Can Robeson County register of deeds staff advise me on a deed?
faqs.a: No. State statute bars the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and the office has no forms. Take drafting questions, including how to word a conveyance, to an attorney before the signing.

faqs.q: What if a deed is mailed to Robeson County without certification?
faqs.a: The office returns it to the sender. Every deed needs tax certification or the delinquent tax statement before it can be recorded.

faqs.q: What is the route to tax certification for a Robeson deed?
faqs.a: Email deeds@robesoncountync.gov, mail the document to the Tax Department at 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton, or phone 910-671-3060 for instructions.

faqs.q: Does Robeson County charge for mailing back a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Yes, $1.00, when you record in person and provide no addressed, stamped return envelope. The document must also carry a return name and mailing address.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer owe the excise tax in Robeson County?
faqs.a: It is the seller's. The tax is $1.00 per $500 of value and is paid to the register before the deed is recorded.
